'''Minor healing mead''' is a [[Black Forest]]-tier consumable item [[Fermenter|fermented]] from '''Mead base: Minor healing'''. == Recipe == ''Mead base: Minor healing'' is produced in a [[Mead Ketill]] with: *{{Item_Link|Honey|10}} *{{Item_Link|Blueberries|5}} *{{Item_Link|Raspberries|10}} *{{Item_Link|Dandelion|1}} Six ''Minor healing meads'' are produced by [[Fermenter|fermenting]] the mead base for two in-game [[Day and Night Cycle|days]]. == Effect == Upon consumption, it restores 50 [[health]] over 10 seconds. A 2-min cooldown is applied preventing consumption of another healing mead. ==Other locations== Other than brewing, {{PAGENAME}}s can be found: * In [[Loot chest#Infested Mine Treasure Ches|treasure chests]] at [[Infested Mine]]s. * Destroyed [[Ancient Pot]]s may drop them. ==See also== *[[Medium Healing Mead]] *[[Major Healing Mead]] *[[Lingering Healing Mead]] {{FoodsNav}} [[cs:Drobná léčivá medovina]] [[ru:Малая медовуха лечения]]

{{infobox structure | appearance = Cooking station appearance.png | description = | id = piece_cookingstation | type = Crafting | usage = Cooking | durability = 20 | size = 1x2 | rain damage = no | materials = * [[Wood]] x2 | effects = |resistances=cooking | support = wood}} The '''Cooking Station''' is used to cook raw meat type ingredients into their cooked form, or if left too long, into [[Coal]]. For the meat to be cooked it is necessary to have a [[Campfire]], [[Hearth]] or [[Hanging Brazier]] underneath the cooking station. It is possible to stack seven cooking stations in a row over a single campfire. This number increases to 10 if the cooking stations are placed halfway inside the campfire. == Recipes and cook length ==

'''Serpent Stew''' is a [[Swamp]]-tier food. 

== Recipe ==
''Serpent Stew'' is produced in a level 2 [[Cauldron]] with:

* {{Item link|Mushroom|1}}
* {{Item link|Cooked Serpent Meat|1}}
* {{Item link|Honey|2}}

As of the Hearth & Home update, to cook Serpent Stew, it is required to have a Cauldron with at least one upgrade, such as the [[Spice Rack]] (which is normally the easiest one to craft).

== Notes ==
* Serpent Stew provides very high health compared to most other food items in its tier at 80, and continues to be a useful food source all the way into the [[Mistlands]].
* Serpent Stew is also tied with [[Meat Platter]] and [[Honey Glazed Chicken]] in terms of health and stamina gain, but falls short in its healing, with the two Mistlands-tier foods healing for 5 hp/tick, whereas Serpent Stew heals for 4 hp/tick.
* Despite being made from Cooked Serpent Meat which weighs 10 units, the stew only weighs 1 unit.

Fermenters are [[Player base|base]] structures used for fermenting mead and wine bases into meads and wines.

They require a roof and 70% [[cover]] to function. Destroying a fermenter will not return the mead or wine base.
== Recipes ==
The [[Mead Ketill]] can be used to brew mead bases, which are fermented into mead. All mead and wine bases result in six finished products except [[Mead base: Berserkir]], which results in three. A fermenter cycle takes 2,400 seconds (40 minutes).

'''Meads''' are items which can be consumed for temporary health and stamina boosts, as well as preventing harmful [[status effects]]. Mead must first be crafted into a mead base at a [[Mead Ketill]] and then fermented using a [[Fermenter]]. Mead can be consumed with or without a [[Tankard]], [[Dvergr Tankard]] or a [[Horn of Celebration]]. ==Cooldown== Meads have ''cooldown'' during which a player cannot drink another mead of the same type. The '''Iron Cooking Station''' is used to cook raw meat type ingredients into their cooked form, or if left too long, into [[Coal]]. For the meat to be cooked, it is necessary to have a [[Hearth]] or two [[Campfire]]s underneath the iron cooking station.

An Iron Cooking Station can be used to cook all meat, including those meats too large for a regular [[Cooking Station]]. Due to the size of the iron cooking station, it is slightly less space-efficient to cook smaller meats than the cooking station. 

Up to five pieces of meat can be cooked at once on the Iron Cooking Station.

The '''Stone Oven''' is used to cook prepped uncooked foods.

The oven has two inputs. The lower input is for [[Wood]] and the upper input is for the recipe ingredient. It can hold 10 wood and bake up to four items at once. Each wood lasts 2000 seconds, or about 33 minutes as fuel, meaning a fully fuelled stone oven will burn for approximately five and a half hours, before running out of fuel. Smoke is emitted while it's lit. Baking takes about 50 seconds with an active fire. If left for more than 100 seconds, the baked item turns to [[Coal]]. 

== Building ==
The stone oven recipe is unlocked only when the player smelts [[Iron]] for the first time and has built an [[Artisan Table]]. To build the Stone Oven, the player must be within the range of an Artisan Table.

Each recipe takes 50 seconds to cook, and will burn into [[Coal]] after 100 seconds.

'''Feasts''' are large meals that last longer and can be shared among several people. Feasts are crafted at the [[Food Preparation Table]] and require spices bought from [[The Bog Witch]]. Before being eaten, they must be placed using the [[Serving Tray]]. They can be placed on any surface, on the floor or on a table, this is done using the Serving Tray build menu to choose which feast to place. Once placed, the feast has 10 servings, and each serving lasts 50 minutes. When all servings are eaten, the empty platter must be removed using the Serving Tray's "Remove" function. If a feast has already been partially eaten, it yields nothing when destroyed or dismantled. Feasts are balanced foods, providing equal amounts of [[health]] and [[stamina]].
